# Welcome to PowerScroll

A visual notebook that lives in **one editable HTML file**. This page is a canvas; the columns on it are **scrolls**, each a named vertical workstream with its own title.

## Try four things

- Double-click this text to edit the Markdown
- Press **T**, then click the canvas to add a block
- Drag the bar at the right of a scroll title to make the scroll wider
- Press **P** and draw; the pen has pressure and an eraser

Press **Ctrl+S** when you want to keep your notebook. Everything, editor included, is written to one file.

## What a scroll is for

Give a scroll to a topic, a week, or a person. The outline in the sidebar lists every scroll on the page, and an agent can be told which scroll to write into.

| Do this | With |
|---|---|
| Rename a scroll | double-click its title |
| Add a scroll | **+ New scroll** in the sidebar |
| Move or delete one | right-click its title |

# Work with an agent

Run `npx -y powerscroll-mcp`, then turn on **Settings → Agent bridge → Let a local agent write into this notebook**. Your agent can read this page, add blocks, place images, and draw editable diagrams like the one below.

## A useful first prompt

```text
Read the open PowerScroll page. In the "Agent workspace" scroll, add a short
plan for the next three steps and draw a Mermaid flowchart of them.
```

Agent edits use the same undo history and the same save path as yours.

# Telemetry gateway

Store-and-forward for the field units. Each unit publishes over MQTT; the gateway buffers when the uplink drops and replays in order once it returns.

## Open points

- [x] Broker sizing for 400 units at 1 Hz
- [x] Replay ordering across reconnects
- [ ] Buffer overflow policy: drop oldest, or refuse new?

| Link | Rate | Budget |
|---|---|---|
| Unit to gateway | 1 Hz | 12 kB/s |
| Gateway to storage | burst | 2 MB/s |

## Decision log

**2026-09-02** Drop-oldest chosen for the overflow policy: the newest state is worth more than the oldest history for this fleet.

Math renders too: the ring holds $t = \frac{S}{r \cdot f}$ seconds of frames for a buffer of $S$ bytes at $r$ bytes per frame and $f$ frames per second.

# Whiteboard

No columns here: this page has its guide style set to **none**, so it is an open canvas. Shapes, arrows, ink and text can go anywhere.

## Notes

- The ink strokes here were drawn with the pen tool; the eraser cuts them
- Arrows bind to shapes; drag a shape and its arrows follow
- Press **1** to **6** to pick a shape, then draw it
